notes:
Stage: procurement. Mid-market product org (customer-facing chat + search) evaluating move from Hosted -> Dedicated for unit economics. POC on hosted API performed; now negotiating Dedicated commit/packaging. Key priorities: predictable per-token unit cost, burst headroom for weekly spikes (product launches), strong audit logging + SSO, and clear ramp schedule to avoid over-commit early.

POC takeaways:
- Latency: 90th ~180ms on hosted; target production SLO 150ms after Dedicated tuning.
- Cost: currently above target; Dedicated expected to reduce unit cost ~30% at 12m commit.
- Model preferences: open-model variants with fallback to smaller architectures when cost constrained.

Pricing/packaging asks from Valence:
- Commit structure: prefer 12-month with quarterly ramp (25% -> 50% -> 75% -> 100%) to ease cashflow.
- Burst: need guaranteed 30% burst capacity over baseline with metering per 1-hour window.
- Overage: want cap or stepped overage rate (1.2x first bracket, 1.5x after threshold) instead of flat 1.6x.
- Ramp credits: request first-month ramp credits if usage < baseline.

Procurement path & stakeholders:
- Decision maker: VP Product (Anika Shah) + CTO (Ravi Patel).
- Procurement owner: Head of Ops (Caleb Moore).
- Legal: Jane Elliott (internal counsel) submitted DPA redlines.
- Timeline: aiming to finalize by 2026-04 for Q2 launch.

Open items for Redwood:
- Confirm burst metering window and exact overage formula so finance can model ARR impact.
- Provide per-route latency SLOs post-Dedicated tuning and example ramp schedule with costs.
- Respond to DPA redlines or propose compromise language on liability and data residency.

Quoted from call: 'We need confidence that the Dedicated commit won't leave us overpaying in ramp months — can we get credits or a gentle ramp?' — VP Product.

Short next steps: sales to propose revised pricing with phased ramp + capped overage; SE to produce expected latency/cost profile for the proposed commit levels; legal to address DPA redlines.
